course_name_en: Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Technology 1
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics, especially: Fundamentals of analysis and linear algebra; Basic knowledge of differential equations (ordinary differential equations, solution methods)

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding the fundamental thermodynamic and fluid dynamic principles and laws
Application of thermodynamic equations to calculate state changes and energy conversion processes
Grasping, systematizing, and quantitatively answering fluid dynamic problems
Analysis and evaluation of technical systems such as power plants, heat pumps, cooling systems, and internal combustion engines
Analysis, evaluation, and optimization of fluid dynamic products, components, and systems in process, chemical engineering, automotive, and energy industries

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Thermodynamics and basic concepts
State variables and equations of state
First Law of Thermodynamics (Conservation of Energy)
Second Law of Thermodynamics (Entropy and Irreversibility)
Thermodynamic cycles
Gas and steam power processes
Refrigerant cycles and heat pumps
Thermodynamic material properties and diagrams
Heat transfer
Properties of fluids, interaction forces in fluids and differentiation from solid bodies and point/solid body mechanics
Equation of motion for one-dimensional flows with friction
Special case of stationary incompressible and compressible fluids:
Hydrostatic fundamental law and technical applications
Pressure profiles in stationary fluids and resulting force effects
Static buoyancy
Concept of streamline/streamtube for one-dimensional description
Description of moving incompressible dissipative fluids with work input or extraction:
Continuity equation
Ideal and extended Bernoulli equation: concept of control volume
Balance-based description of turbomachinery
Pipe hydraulics in linear flow systems: calculation of flow losses in laminar and turbulent flows
Empirical description of bodies in flow using coefficients, airfoil theory and aerodynamics of blunt bodies

assessment_methods.method: Examination prerequisite (Fluid Mechanics) as written examination/test or oral examination

assessment_rules: The written examination/test for Thermodynamics (MECB411D) over 90 minutes determines the module grade for MECB410D. For Fluid Mechanics (MECB412D), an examination prerequisite is required, either as a 60-minute written examination/test or a 20-minute oral examination. The specific form of this prerequisite will be announced at the beginning of the course.
